**Definition**: An extension to the base framework that uses PN-triangles and displacement mapping to voxelize low-resolution meshes with rugged surfaces at high resolution, achieving visual quality comparable to conventional voxelization of high-resolution meshes [S1, unofficial].

The claim accurately reflects the content of Source [S1]. The source explicitly states that the extension (displacement voxelization) uses PN-triangles and displacement mapping to voxelize low-resolution meshes, achieving visual quality comparable to conventional voxelization of high-resolution meshes.
Use PN-triangles to reconstruct mesh details [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that 'positions and normals of PNtriangles are used to reconstruct the details of the mesh' and notes that this is part of an extension using PN-triangles. This directly supports the claim.
Displacement voxelization was developed to maintain visual quality while achieving higher performance by voxelizing low-resolution versions of triangle meshes [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that displacement voxelization was developed to maintain visual quality while achieving higher performance by voxelizing low-resolution versions of triangle meshes. The evidence explicitly states: 'While higher performance can be achieved by voxelizing a lowresolution version of the triangle mesh, this would introduce visible artifacts. To maintain the quality of voxelization while achieving higher performance, we develop an extension called displacement voxelization.' It further confirms that the result on a low-resolution mesh is visually comparable to high-resolution conventional voxelization. Thus, all facts in the claim are present and supported by the evidence.
**Steps**: Perform triangle subdivision using the hardware tessellator as in the base method [S1, unofficial].

Source [S1] explicitly lists 'Perform triangle subdivision using the hardware tessellator as in the base method' as a key feature and confirms in the passage that 'displacement mapping [3] is introduced after the triangle subdivision process'. Therefore, the evidence fully supports the claim.
Utilize the positions and normals of the PN-triangles to apply displacement mapping during the voxelization process [S1, unofficial].
